findings.detail: The portfolio volatility of {{m:risk.vol.pct}} exceeds the maximum threshold of {{m:risk.vol_band_max.pct}} for a conservative investor. Given the client is {{m:age}} and requires monthly income, this elevated volatility poses a significant risk to capital preservation and liquidity needs.
findings.title: Portfolio volatility exceeds conservative suitability band

findings.detail: The holding in NRTH represents {{m:conc.NRTH.pct}} of the portfolio, significantly exceeding the {{m:conc.limit.pct}} concentration limit. This high exposure to a single security creates excessive idiosyncratic risk, which is inappropriate for a conservative retiree.
findings.title: Excessive concentration in single security NRTH

findings.detail: In an equity bear market scenario, the portfolio is projected to lose {{m:stress.equity_bear.cad}}, representing a {{m:stress.equity_bear.pct}} decline. This potential loss is substantial for a conservative client drawing monthly income, potentially impacting their long-term financial stability.
findings.title: Significant downside risk in equity bear market scenario
No unused TFSA contribution room available
findings.detail: The client has no unused TFSA contribution room ({{m:tax.tfsa_room.cad}}), limiting opportunities to optimize tax-sheltered growth. All current contributions are maximized.
The client has no unused RRSP contribution room ({{m:tax.rrsp_room.cad}}), meaning no additional tax-deferred savings can be made at this time.
findings.title: No unused RRSP contribution room available

findings.detail: US equity holdings experienced significant growth, with the index returning {{m:mkt.us_equity_ytd.pct}} percent year to date, driven by a rally in technology names.
findings.title: US equity growth driven by technology sector rally
Canadian bond yields decline amid cooling inflation
findings.detail: Canadian bond yields have drifted lower to {{m:mkt.ca_10y_yield.pct}} percent as inflation cools, contributing to a year to date return of {{m:mkt.ca_bond_ytd.pct}} percent for the Canadian bond index.

findings.title: Significant Canadian equity overweight driven by concentrated holding
findings.detail: Canadian equity is significantly overweight by {{m:drift.CA_EQUITY.pp}} percentage points, primarily due to the concentrated position in Northshore Energy ({{m:acct.NON_REG.value.cad}} in NON_REG). This exceeds the drift tolerance of {{m:cfg.drift_tolerance.pp}} percentage points, creating a critical risk to the conservative mandate.

US equity is underweight by {{m:drift.US_EQUITY.pp}} percentage points, exceeding the {{m:cfg.drift_tolerance.pp}} percentage point tolerance. This drift, combined with the Canadian equity concentration, indicates a portfolio structure that deviates from the conservative risk profile.
findings.title: US equity underweight relative to conservative model portfolio
